$comment: Foundry-owned append-preserving identity lifecycle operation. Not ASA authority. These records live in the registry's identity-operations journal rather than inside a UAO, because uid is a pure function of resolution_key: two uids can never become one by rewriting, so merge and split can only exist as a mapping layer above the derivation. SUPERSEDE and RETIRE additionally have ASA-governed canonical representations (lifecycle_status plus successor_identity_ref) which a future manufacture may carry; this journal records the governed decision, not a rewrite of any immutable package.
title: UAO Foundry Identity Operation

operationId.$comment: Content address over the meaning-bearing projection, so the record is self-verifying and cannot be edited in place.

subjects.$comment: Registered identities the operation acts upon. Every subject must already exist in the registry; an operation may not act on an identity that was never manufactured.

targets.$comment: Resulting identities. Empty for RETIRE, which has no successor by definition.

justification.$comment: Required and non-blank. An identity operation without a stated reason is indistinguishable from a mistake once its author is gone.

authority.$comment: Who decided. The Foundry does not adjudicate authority; it records the claim so an auditor can.
